steps.say: A prefix goes at the front of a word and changes its meaning. The root word keeps its spelling.
Remember the Grade 3 prefixes too. Un- and dis- mean not, and re- means again.
Keep every letter when you join the parts. That is why misspell has two s letters.
Some words only look as if they have a prefix. Cover the start and check that the rest is a word.
steps.show: pretty: tty is not a word

options.why: Pre- means before, and prehear is not a word.

hints: Look at the start of each word.
Cover hear in each word and compare the prefixes.
check.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, so mishear means hear wrongly.

check.prompt:
Add pre- to heat.
Mum will ___ the oven before she bakes the cake.
hints: The oven is heated before the baking starts.
Write the prefix, then the whole word heat.
check.explanation: Pre- means before, so preheat means heat before. Mum heats the oven before baking.
